claims.text: A thin Mo interlayer between W and CuCrZr can reduce thermal stress under extreme thermal cycling.
A thin Mo interlayer between W and CuCrZr can improve interfacial cohesion under extreme thermal cycling.
Directly bonded W/CuCrZr joints typically develop high residual stresses because of thermal-expansion mismatch.
Directly bonded W/CuCrZr joints are susceptible to delamination.
The proposed intervention is a controlled-thickness Mo interlayer, on the order of tens of micrometers, between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed W/Mo/CuCrZr joint is intended for high-heat-flux cycling conditions encountered in fusion reactors.
The proposed W/Mo/CuCrZr joint is intended for neutron-irradiation conditions encountered in fusion reactors.
Mo has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
An intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient allows the Mo layer to serve as a transition between W and CuCrZr.
The Mo transition layer alleviates stress concentration at the W/CuCrZr interface.
Mo has a high melting point.
Mo's thermal-expansion behavior reduces interfacial thermal mismatch in a W/Mo/CuCrZr joint.
Reduced interfacial thermal mismatch decreases microcracking and delamination during rapid thermal cycling.
Compared with a direct W/CuCrZr bond, the Mo-containing joint will exhibit reduced crack propagation during repeated thermal loading.
Compared with a direct W/CuCrZr bond, the Mo-containing joint will exhibit improved bonding integrity during repeated thermal loading.
Compared with a direct W/CuCrZr bond, the Mo-containing joint will exhibit enhanced interfacial heat-transfer efficiency during repeated thermal loading.
W/CuCrZr joints without an interlayer traditionally fail early under extreme operating conditions because of high interfacial stresses.
The benefit of the Mo interlayer depends on its thickness and processing conditions.
Under some neutron-flux conditions, Mo may exhibit behavior that produces additional failure modes.
The magnitude and long-term irradiation stability of the proposed improvement have not yet been experimentally established.
